body.estimand_functional: \(\Omega^Q_{k,m}(\varepsilon)=\sup_{D_H(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\leq\varepsilon}d_Q(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\asymp\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\), uniformly on every fixed nondegenerate bounded class containing the lower family. The auxiliary modulus \(\Omega_{k,m}\) defined through \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}\) has the same order. For \((n,k,m)=(2,2,1)\), the exponent is \(3/4\).

sampling_model.design: One observational environment and two grouped positive stochastic perfect-intervention environments for every latent node; group labels are observed up to one common node permutation.
sampling_model.units: \(N\) independent observations from each environment on \(\mathbb T^n\), independent across environments.
sampling_model.treatment: The environment replaces exactly one latent conditional mechanism by a parent-free circular density \(q_i^e\) normalized with respect to \(d\lambda(t)=dt/(2\pi)\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every complete latent law is bounded between \(c_0\) and \(C_0\), and the decoder is uniformly bi-Lipschitz.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Positive Fourier estimation uses cutoff \(L_N\asymp N^{1/(2s_{\mathrm{obs}}+n)}\), floor \(N^{-1}\), and law radius \(\rho_N=N^{-s_{\mathrm{obs}}/(2s_{\mathrm{obs}}+n)}\). A deterministically enumerated rational periodic spline sieve carries interval certificates for positivity, normalization, DAG factorization, finite-type margins, decoder invertibility, and all unchanged class bounds. The fitting and calibration criteria minimize the empirical complete-law orbit distance over the finite common permutation group. Propagation through the sharp modulus yields \(\rho_N^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\); for \((n,k,m)=(2,2,1)\), \(s_{\mathrm{obs}}=1\), so this is \(N^{-3/16}\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Then CauCA in \((G,\mathcal F,\mathcal P_G)\) is identifiable up to \(\mathcal S_{\mathrm{scaling}}\).
Two hard interventions with interventional discrepancy on the same target node suffice to recover that node up to a diffeomorphism.
Then there is \(A\in SO(d)\) such that \(g^{-1}\circ f(s)=As+h(s)+b\).
Algorithms 2 and 3 are consistent estimators of the latent graph and inverse transformation up to the corresponding equivalence classes.
With a large enough \(N\), the estimated cross-derivative vectors are almost zero for all coordinate pairs.

body.tldr: Complete paired interventions identify a synthetic product law and determinant--ratio residual. The arbitrary-map strip-to-corner inequality now proves the sharp full-class modulus \(\Omega^Q_{k,m}(\varepsilon)\asymp\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\) for the intrinsic probability-integral-gauge encoder quotient, with the older \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}\) retained only as an auxiliary aligned discrepancy. The primary two-node \(C^2\) Morse exponent is \(3/4\). A finite certified spectral/spline procedure propagates the sharp modulus, giving primary representation rate \(N^{-3/16}\), and its permutation-compatible inverted law ball is honest with the same intrinsic quotient diameter.

project_justification.gap: Exact CauCA and score-change results do not quantify nonzero complete-law perturbations at isolated critical points, and prescribed-Jacobian or near-isometry rigidity does not supply the determinant-plus-degenerate-ratio inequality needed here.
project_justification.niche: Circular probability-integral gauges convert arbitrary latent reparameterizations into rotations or reflections, while paired interventions expose both the scalar profile residuals and a synthetic determinant channel. The finite-type critical geometry then reduces arbitrary mixed motion to two-coordinate critical corners.
project_justification.fill: The note proves the synthetic product reduction, the arbitrary-field weighted coercivity estimate, nonlinear determinant absorption, the matching full-class inverse modulus, and the audited \(3/4\) Morse case. It also gives an evaluable finite recovery sieve and a permutation-orbit confidence set whose intrinsic diameter inherits the sharp exponent.

body.related_work: Liang et al. and Varıcı et al. occupy exact componentwise recovery and plateau or almost-everywhere regimes, but neither supplies a nonzero-error full-law modulus. Buchholz and Schölkopf control a near-isometry defect rather than determinant distortion coupled to Morse-degenerate scalar transports. Prescribed-Jacobian and volume-correction results motivate the determinant channel, but the load-bearing strip-to-corner coefficient elimination is proved here directly and avoids an endpoint Hodge estimate. Compact-manifold density estimation supports the law-radius rung; the causal exponent and intrinsic quotient propagation follow from the new finite-type incompressible-rigidity theorem.
body.interpretation: The localized Hamiltonian family and the arbitrary-map upper inequality now meet. A law perturbation of size \(\varepsilon\) permits, and uniformly limits, canonical encoder motion of order \(\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\). The dimension-free power is caused by two-coordinate critical corners: the \(C^k\) remainder contributes \(h^k\), their square-root volume contributes \(h\), and the order-\(m\) profile contributes the extra \(h^m\). Probability-integral canonicalization makes this a statement about an invariant quotient rather than a chosen latent gauge.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Constants are uniform only on a fixed nondegenerate class with the stated positivity, \(C^k\), decoder-conditioning, critical-cardinality, critical-separation, finite-type margin, and attained-order constants. The result does not cover plateaus, coalescing critical points below \(\Delta_0\), support holes, unbounded decoder condition numbers, vector-valued turning contrast curves, or unknown-order adaptation without an additional testing-separation analysis. The older symmetric aligned discrepancy is controlled by the intrinsic quotient distance but is not used to characterize quotient equivalence.
body.honest_scope: The population claim is the sharp full-class identity \(\Omega^Q_{k,m}(\varepsilon)\asymp\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\) on each fixed nondegenerate bounded class containing the lower family; the same order holds for the auxiliary \(\Omega_{k,m}\). For \((n,k,m)=(2,2,1)\), the exponent is \(3/4\), and with \(\rho_N=N^{-1/4}\) the certified estimator and intrinsic quotient confidence diameter have rate \(N^{-3/16}\). Coverage is simultaneous over the empirical complete-law permutation orbit and includes deterministic Fourier bias and finite-sieve tolerance. No claim is made for plateaus, absent critical spacing, support failure, unbounded decoders, vector-valued profiles, or adaptation across unknown critical orders.
